questions.question: The imbalance that labour law answers is that:
options: A firm can survive a vacancy longer than an applicant can survive without wages — so the law lays floors, wraps procedures, and adds collective strength behind the weaker party
Workers always earn more than owners
Employers cannot dismiss anyone
Markets automatically produce fair contracts

questions.question: Alongside workers' rights, the Constitution gives employers the mirror rights to:
options: Set wages by decree
Form employers' organisations and, within the law, lock workers out
Ban all union membership
Ignore collective agreements

questions.question: SELF-GOVERNMENT as a principle of the LRA means:
options: Every worker signs an individual deal
The state fixes all wages annually
Organised workers and employers negotiate the terms of their own relationship — the state builds the arena but does not dictate the wage
Firms govern their unions

questions.question: CONSULTATION as a principle requires that:
options: Unions approve every hire
Workers vote on company strategy
The state attend every meeting
Employers consult and disclose information before decisions that land on workers — retrenchment being the heaviest

questions.question: The LRA performs the job of:
options: Rules of ENGAGEMENT — union rights, bargaining institutions, protected strikes and lock-outs, unfair dismissal, and the CCMA and Labour Courts
Setting the minimum leave entitlements
Paying injured workers
Collecting employment taxes

questions.question: The BCEA's provisions include:
options: Sector-wide wage extensions
Maximum ordinary hours, overtime multipliers, four kinds of minimum leave, notice periods, and bans on child and forced labour
Rules for calling a strike
The design of the compensation fund

questions.question: The floor-never-ceiling rule states that:
options: No contract may exceed BCEA conditions
The BCEA overrides better offers
A contract may IMPROVE on the floor, but no signature can lower it
Floors apply only to union members

questions.question: The bargain built into COIDA is:
options: Workers insure themselves privately
Employers pay only after losing in court
The fund pays only where negligence is proven
The worker claims from the employer-financed fund WITHOUT suing or proving negligence; the contributing employer is shielded from individual damages claims

questions.question: Collective bargaining fuses:
options: Many powerless individual bargains into one bargain with weight — representatives negotiating wages, hours and conditions for all
Unions and employers into one body
Wages and profits into one account
All sectors into one economy-wide deal

questions.question: A bargaining council agreement can be EXTENDED, meaning:
options: It lasts longer than a year
It can bind the entire SECTOR — even firms that sat outside the negotiating room — so one floor holds for all competitors
It automatically covers other sectors
It becomes part of the Constitution

questions.question: A workplace forum differs from a union because it:
options: Negotiates sector wages
Calls protected strikes
Is elected by ALL workers of one large workplace — unionised or not — and its mandate is CONSULTATION, not wage negotiation
Represents the employer's side

questions.question: The three chambers and their conversations are:
options: Conciliation, mediation, arbitration
LRA, BCEA, COIDA
Labour Court, Appeal Court, CCMA
Union organises and negotiates; bargaining council convenes sector-level negotiation; workplace forum consults within one workplace

subtopics.title: When Talks Fail — the CCMA and the Courts

questions.question: In CONCILIATION at the CCMA:
options: The commissioner steers the parties toward their OWN settlement — chairing and testing positions; nothing is forced on anyone
The commissioner issues a binding award
Lawyers must argue formally
The employer chooses the outcome

questions.question: The step MEDIATION adds beyond conciliation is that the go-between:
options: Decides the dispute finally
Actively PUTS FORWARD possible solutions — which either side may still take or leave
Refers the matter straight to court
Suspends the right to strike

questions.question: ARBITRATION concludes with:
options: A voluntary handshake
A referral back to mediation
An AWARD — the commissioner hears both sides' evidence and issues a ruling that binds the parties
A secret ballot of workers

questions.question: A strike is PROTECTED when:
options: It lasts less than a day
A court approves it in advance
The majority of the public supports it
The procedures were honoured — dispute referred, notice delivered — shielding strikers from dismissal for striking; without them the shield falls away

questions.question: Thabo's complaint alone barely lands because:
options: The supervisor weighs one replaceable packer against the queue at the fence
Complaints must be written
Wages are set by the Constitution
Supervisors may not receive complaints

questions.question: When every packer stands at the door with one spokesperson, the supervisor now weighs:
options: One worker against another
An entire warehouse falling silent against the orders that must ship — separate whispers gathered into one voice that carries
The cost of hiring more supervisors
The queue against the fence

questions.question: The state's position in the contest is:
options: Star player for the workers
Owner of the warehouse
REFEREE — writing the rules of the match and whistling fouls, but never scoring the goals: self-government
Coach of the employers

questions.question: The three rulebooks match three kinds of day:
options: The ARGUMENT day (LRA), the ORDINARY day (BCEA), and the WORST day (COIDA)
Payday, holiday, birthday
Hiring day, promotion day, retirement day
Court day, strike day, election day

questions.question: A weekend job offering terms beneath the BCEA floor is:
options: Valid once the worker signs
UNLAWFUL the moment the offer is made — whatever is signed, the floor cannot be contracted away
Legal for part-time work only
A matter the union must first approve

questions.question: On the worst day, COIDA provides that:
options: The worker must sue and prove fault
Only permanent staff are covered
The worker or the family claims from the employer-financed fund — medical bills, disability support, dependants' benefits — with no court case required
The union pays the medical bills

questions.question: "Identify the day, and the Act names itself" is a method for:
options: Planning the working week
Calculating leave days
Choosing which union to join
Sorting scenario questions onto the correct statute by asking what KIND of day the scenario describes

subtopics.title: The Ladder in the Referee's Room

questions.question: The three rungs, separated by who decides:
options: Conciliation — the parties alone; mediation — the parties, choosing among proposals; arbitration — the COMMISSIONER, whose ruling binds
The referee decides on every rung
The courts decide on every rung
The employer decides unless outvoted

questions.question: The ladder exhausts self-agreement before imposing because:
options: Arbitration is too expensive to run
An agreement the parties built is honoured willingly, while an imposed outcome is merely endured — and many disputes were misunderstandings wearing angry faces
The law forbids arbitration in most cases
Referees prefer not to work

questions.question: Above the referee's room stand:
options: The bargaining councils
The employers' organisations
The LABOUR COURT — reviewing awards and ruling on the law — with the Labour Appeal Court above it
The compensation fund trustees

questions.question: "Skip the rungs, and the strike walks naked" means:
options: Strikes are always dismissable offences
Strikers must wear uniforms
Lock-outs are never permitted
A strike called without the required procedures is UNPROTECTED — its strikers lose the shield against dismissal for striking
